items.prompt: What is the defining feature that gives mammals their name?

options.label: Having a backbone
options.feedback: A backbone is a trait of all vertebrates, not unique to mammals. The name comes from a different feature.

options.label: Milk-producing mammary glands
options.feedback: Correct. The word 'mammal' comes from the Latin for breast, and these glands feed the young with milk.

options.label: Being warm-blooded
options.feedback: Being warm-blooded is a shared trait with birds, so it is not the defining feature named after the breast.

options.label: Living on land
options.feedback: Many mammals live in water or fly, so land living is not a defining trait. The name refers to milk glands.

items.ok_line: Mammary glands are the core feature.
items.ko_line: The name points to milk production.
items.exp_text: All mammals have milk-producing mammary glands, which is where the name comes from. This is the key trait that separates them from reptiles and birds.

items.prompt: Which of these is a feature found in mammals but not in reptiles or birds?

options.label: Scales
options.feedback: Scales are typical of reptiles and fish, not mammals. Mammals have fur or hair instead.

options.label: Feathers
options.feedback: Feathers belong to birds, not mammals. Mammals have hair or fur covering their bodies.

options.label: Three middle ear bones
options.feedback: Correct. These three small bones are unique to mammals and help with hearing.

options.label: Being able to fly
options.feedback: Bats are mammals that fly, but birds also fly, so this is not a defining mammal feature.

items.ko_line: That trait is shared with other classes.
items.exp_text: Mammals have three middle ear bones, which reptiles and birds do not have. This is one of the traits that sets them apart.

items.prompt: What do all mammals have on their bodies, even if it is not always thick?

options.label: Fur or hair
options.feedback: Correct. All mammals have fur or hair at some stage of life, though it can be thin or sparse in some.

options.label: Scales
options.feedback: Scales are found on reptiles and fish, not mammals. Mammals grow fur or hair.

options.label: Feathers
options.feedback: Feathers are exclusive to birds. Mammals are covered with hair or fur.

options.label: A shell
options.feedback: Shells are seen on turtles and some invertebrates, not on mammals. Mammals have fur or hair.

items.ok_line: Fur or hair is universal in mammals.
items.ko_line: That covering belongs to other animal groups.
items.exp_text: Every mammal has fur or hair at some point in its life. Even whales have some hair, usually around the mouth or as whiskers.

items.prompt: Which group of mammals lays eggs instead of giving birth to live young?

options.label: Placentals
options.feedback: Placentals give birth to live young and have a placenta. They do not lay eggs.

options.label: Marsupials
options.feedback: Marsupials give birth to very small live young that finish growing in a pouch. They do not lay eggs.

options.label: Cetaceans
options.feedback: Whales and dolphins are placentals and give birth to live young in the water. They do not lay eggs.

options.label: Monotremes
options.feedback: Correct. Monotremes, like the platypus, are the only mammals that lay eggs.

items.ko_line: Those groups give birth to live young.
items.exp_text: There are only five species of monotremes, and they lay eggs. All other modern mammals give birth to live young.

items.prompt: What is the function of the placenta in most mammals?

options.label: To help the mother breathe
options.feedback: The mother breathes with her own lungs, not the placenta. The placenta feeds the developing young.

options.label: To feed the developing young
options.feedback: Correct. The placenta lets the offspring draw nutrition from the mother during gestation.

options.label: To protect the mother from predators
options.feedback: The placenta is inside the mother's body and does not protect her. It nourishes the embryo or fetus.

options.label: To store fat for the mother
options.feedback: Fat storage is done in body tissues, not the placenta. The placenta supplies nutrients to the young.

items.ok_line: The placenta feeds the growing offspring.
items.ko_line: The placenta has a different job.
items.exp_text: The placenta is a temporary organ that delivers nutrients from the mother to the developing young during gestation. This is why placental mammals are the most species-rich.

items.prompt: Which order of mammals has the most species?

options.label: Bats
options.feedback: Bats are the second largest order, but they are not the largest. The largest is the one with gnawing mammals.

options.label: Primates
options.feedback: Primates are only the fourth largest order. The largest order is made up of gnawing mammals.

options.label: Rodents
options.feedback: Correct. Rodents, including mice and rats, form the largest order of mammals by number of species.

options.label: Carnivora
options.feedback: Carnivora, like cats and dogs, is the sixth largest order. Rodents are the largest.

items.ok_line: Rodents are the most numerous order.
items.ko_line: That order has fewer species than rodents.
items.exp_text: Rodents have the most species among all mammal orders, followed by bats and then eulipotyphlans like shrews and moles.

items.prompt: How do most mammals move on land?

options.label: On four limbs
options.feedback: Correct. The basic mammal body type is quadrupedal, using four limbs for walking or running.

options.label: On two limbs only
options.feedback: Only some mammals are bipedal, like humans and kangaroos. Most use four limbs.

options.label: By slithering
options.feedback: Slithering is how snakes move, not typical of mammals. Most mammals walk on four legs.

options.label: By hopping on one leg
options.feedback: No mammal moves on one leg. Most use four limbs for terrestrial locomotion.

items.exp_text: Most mammals walk or run on four limbs. Some have adapted those limbs for swimming, flying, climbing, or digging.

items.prompt: What do mammals use to communicate?

options.label: Only loud calls
options.feedback: Mammals use many forms of communication, not just loud calls. They also use sounds, scents, and body language.

options.label: Only body movement
options.feedback: Movement is one way, but mammals also use sounds and smells. Communication is multi-modal.

options.label: Only visual signals
options.feedback: Visual signals are used, but mammals also rely on scent and vocal sounds to communicate.

options.label: Sounds, smells, and body language
options.feedback: Correct. Mammals communicate through vocalizations, scent marking, and various postures or movements.

items.ko_line: Communication is not limited to one kind.
items.exp_text: Mammals can make sounds like singing or alarm calls, leave scent marks, and use body language. Some even use echolocation or complex language in humans.

items.prompt: Which of these animals is a monotreme?

options.label: Kangaroo
options.feedback: A kangaroo is a marsupial, not a monotreme. Monotremes are the egg-laying mammals.

options.label: Platypus
options.feedback: Correct. The platypus is one of the five species of monotremes that lay eggs.

options.label: Dolphin
options.feedback: A dolphin is a placental mammal that gives birth to live young, not a monotreme.

options.label: Bat
options.feedback: A bat is a placental mammal, not a monotreme. Monotremes lay eggs.

items.ko_line: That animal belongs to a different group.
items.exp_text: Platypuses are monotremes, one of only five egg-laying mammal species. Other monotremes are echidnas.

items.prompt: What is the study of mammals called?

options.label: Ornithology
options.feedback: Ornithology is the study of birds, not mammals. The study of mammals has a different name.

options.label: Herpetology
options.feedback: Herpetology is the study of reptiles and amphibians. Mammals are studied in a separate field.

options.label: Mammalogy
options.feedback: Correct. Mammalogy is the scientific study of mammals.

options.label: Entomology
options.feedback: Entomology is the study of insects, not mammals. The correct term is mammalogy.

items.ko_line: That field studies a different animal group.
items.exp_text: Mammalogy is the branch of biology dedicated to studying mammals, including their anatomy, behavior, and evolution.
